sources.entry: Redis.app - The easiest way to get started with Redis on the Mac.

summary.one_liner: Redis.app is a macOS app that bundles Redis binaries so you can run a Redis server on a Mac by dragging the app into Applications.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Redis.app as a drag-and-drop way to get Redis running on a Mac: download, move to the Applications folder, and double-click. The app bundles Redis binaries inside its Contents/Resources/Vendor/redis/bin directory. The README explains that release version numbers track the bundled Redis version, with a separate build number for the app itself. It shows how to add those binaries to your shell PATH, either through ~/.bash_profile or through path_helper via /etc/paths.d. It also mentions installing via Homebrew Cask with the redis-app cask. The README is short and does not describe server configuration or a GUI beyond the launch behavior.
use_cases: run a local Redis server on macOS
install Redis on a Mac without building from source
make redis-server and redis-cli available on the command line
set up a local Redis for development
how_to_run: Download Redis.app (download link in README; the link text is empty in the README)
Drag Redis.app to the Applications folder
Or install with: brew cask install redis-app
notable: Drag-and-drop install: no build step needed
Version numbers follow the bundled Redis version, with a separate app build number
Bundled Redis binaries can be added to PATH via shell profile or path_helper
Available through Homebrew Cask as redis-app
caveats: README gives no details on configuration, supported macOS versions, or Redis version included
Download link text is empty in the README, so the download location is not stated explicitly
keywords: start redis without building from source
